items.title: Trump softens threat against Bombardier with thousands of jobs at stake in Mississauga
items.summary: S. President Donald Trump appears to be backing away from his threat to block Bombardier aircraft sales in the United States, a move that could ease concerns for the aerospace manufacturer’s major operations in Mississauga. Trump signalled the change in position during a rally in Kansas on Monday (Oct. 19), saying he would help the Canadian aircraft maker after learning more about its American workforce. “I always viewed them as a Canadian company,” Trump said, adding that the United States would not hurt the company if it had operations in Kansas. “We’ll take care of those people, all right, and the jobs,” he said. S. market, according to media reports. The potential reversal comes after Trump targeted the Quebec-based manufacturer in September, declaring that Bombardier should no longer be allowed to sell its products in the United States unless it moved production there. The threat raised concerns about the impact on Bombardier’s operations on both sides of the border, including its aircraft assembly centre in Mississauga. The facility, located at Toronto Pearson International Airport, employs more than 2,200 people and is one of Ontario’s major aerospace manufacturing operations. The 40-acre campus includes a 770,000-square-foot final assembly building and a pre-flight hangar, according to the Ontario government.

items.title: Cover your plants: Frost advisory issued in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Take preventive measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees and crops, Environment Canada says. Environment and Climate Change Canada issues a frost advisory and is warning residents to cover up sensitive plants. It’s been a sunny and warm week across most of southern Ontario, but a chilly evening looms on Tuesday. Environment and Climate Change Canada has issued a yellow level frost advisory for Mississauga and Brampton, warning residents that patchy frost is expected tonight, mainly in areas away from Lake Ontario. The frost advisory extends to St. Catharines, Grimsby and Northern Niagara. According to Environment Canada, frost can potentially cause damage to plants, trees and crops. The cold temperatures impact leaves, flowers and buds still developing on stems. Gardeners can use plastic containers, sheets or bags to cover up their outdoor plants overnight.

items.title: Weather alert issued for Mississauga, Brampton and Niagara Region
items.summary: A weather alert has been issued for Mississauga, Brampton, and Niagara Region. Environment Canada has issued a yellow frost advisory for the municipalities with chilly conditions expected overnight. In Niagara, St. Catharines, Grimsby, Niagara Falls, and Welland are among the places impacted. Environment Canada said patchy frost is expected, mainly for areas away from the lakes. Forecasters are predicting a low of 1 C overnight in Mississauga, Brampton, St. Catharines, and Niagara Falls. However, as mentioned it’ll be a bit warmer as you get closer to the lakes. Areas shaded in yellow are under a frost advisory from Environment Canada with chilly conditions expected overnight. Frost is expected, particularly for areas away from the lakes. (Credit: Environment Canada) Heading into the day on Wednesday, a high of 16 C and sunny conditions are expected.

items.title: Stabbing of U.S. prison guard adds 50 years to terror sentence of Mississauga man
items.summary: S. prison for plotting terrorist attacks in New York City has been sentenced to another 50 years behind bars after stabbing two correctional officers. Abdulrahman El Bahnasawy, 28, was sentenced on Oct. S. Department of Justice. The additional sentence will run consecutively to his existing 40-year term, bringing his combined prison sentences to 90 years. The attack happened on Dec. 7, 2020, while El Bahnasawy was serving his original sentence for his role in an ISIS-inspired plot targeting heavily populated areas of New York City. According to prosecutors, El Bahnasawy fashioned a weapon from part of a steel desk in his cell and used it to attack two correctional officers. He stabbed one officer in the head and face, then stabbed a second officer in the hand when she intervened. The first officer ultimately lost his right eye as a result of the injuries. ” A pledge of allegiance to ISIS was also found taped inside a locker door in his cell, the Justice Department said. El Bahnasawy pleaded guilty in November 2025 to multiple charges related to the assault, including assault with intent to commit murder, as well as possessing contraband in prison and providing material support to ISIS, a designated foreign terrorist organization.

items.title: Hazel McCallion’s legacy important to some voters as Mississauga election nears: survey
items.summary: Hazel McCallion has been gone for nearly four years, but a recent survey shows some Mississauga voters are thinking about her legacy as they prepare to cast their ballots in the city’s mayoral race next Monday. A Liaison Strategies Mississauga survey conducted earlier this month found that McCallion’s legacy matters to 75 per cent of residents aged 65 and older when choosing a mayor. Additionally, the results show the former longtime mayor’s legacy is a consideration for 29 per cent of those aged 18 to 34. McCallion forged a national — and international — political reputation while serving as Mississauga mayor from 1978 until 2014, when she was succeed by Bonnie Crombie. She died in January 2023 at the age of 101. Results of the Liaison Strategies survey were released as Mississauga residents get ready to vote on Oct. 26 for the city’s next mayor and members of council. ” Overall, regardless of age, 49 per cent of survey respondents said McCallion’s legacy is important while, in response to another question, 52 per cent said a mayoral candidate claiming to have learned from her makes no difference to their support. Survey results were based on a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents from Oct. 2-4.

items.title: Extending subway from Toronto to Mississauga a priority for mayoral candidate
items.summary: Former Mississauga mayor Bonnie Crombie says bringing a subway line to the city will be among her top priorities should voters return her to the office she previously held for a decade. Crombie said today that if she claims victory when the dust settles on election night next Monday, she’ll get things moving on the subway plan within her first 100 days in office. Her goal, Crombie told the media in Mississauga’s downtown core on Tuesday morning, is to extend the TTC’s Line 2 (Bloor-Danforth) west from Kipling to serve Sherway Gardens and then continue into the heart of Mississauga’s City Centre by Square One Shopping Centre. The extension would allow residents to board the subway in Mississauga and “travel directly into Toronto’s subway network,” Crombie, who served as Mississauga mayor from 2014 to 2024 before leaving to lead the Ontario Liberal Party, explained. “Too many people leave home before their children wake up and struggle to get back for dinner,” said Crombie. “Residents deserve more time with their families and better access to jobs and opportunities. ” Crombie, incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and Mississauga city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla are the four main candidates in a field of 14 hopefuls vying for the mayor’s chair in Canada’s seventh-largest city. With record-setting advance polling taking place earlier this month, the remainder of eligible voters in Mississauga will cast their ballots, should they choose to do so, on Oct. 26.

items.title: Joint Business Case, Not a Construction Date, Anchors Crombie's Subway Pitch for Mississauga
items.summary: CityNews Toronto reports Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie has unveiled a plan to push for a western extension of the TTC's Line 2 subway into the city, starting with a joint business case rather than a construction commitment. According to the outlet, Crombie says she would work with the province, Metrolinx, the City of Toronto and the TTC to study extending the line west from Kipling Station through Sherway Gardens and into Mississauga's city centre. The outlet reports the proposal includes no construction timeline or cost estimate, focusing instead on determining whether the project is feasible and how it could be delivered. CityNews says Crombie, if elected, would convene meetings with government and transit partners within her first 100 days and seek federal involvement in the planning process, while also bringing a council motion in that same window to formally launch the city's participation and identify funding for its share. According to the proposal, the study would examine potential routes and station locations, including options near Sherway Gardens and City Centre, along with connections to the Hazel McCallion Line, GO Transit, MiWay and the Mississauga Transitway. The outlet reports the study would also look at ridership, travel-time savings, accessibility, nearby housing and employment growth, construction and operating costs, and environmental impacts. CityNews says Crombie wants the jointly funded study underway within her first year in office, with the initial business case completed within two years.

items.title: October 26 Marks Election Day for Mississauga's Mayor, Council and School Trustees
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents head to the polls on Monday, Oct. 26, to elect the city's next mayor, their ward and regional councillor, and local school board trustees for the 2026 to 2030 term. The city says voters can cast a ballot at any voting location within their own ward rather than being tied to a single assigned site. Officials recommend confirming you're on the voters' list before heading out, since that step can speed up the process at the polls. Anyone who received a voter notification card in September is encouraged to bring it along, though the city notes the card isn't required to vote. What is required, according to the city, is one piece of identification showing your name and a qualifying Mississauga address. The City of Mississauga says it remains committed to accessible voting, and residents looking for details on accommodations can find them through the Ways to Vote page on the city's Mississauga Votes site.

items.title: Displacement Fears at Twin Pines Mobile Home Park Dominate Ward 3 Election Platforms
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports that long-standing fears over displacement at the Twin Pines Mobile Home Park are dominating candidate platforms in Ward 3 ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election. According to the outlet, Peel Region is moving ahead with plans to redevelop the Dundas Street East property into affordable housing, a site that once held more than 200 homes and now has roughly 130 remaining as residents weigh Peel Living's exit offer. The outlet reports many of the long-term residents are seniors on fixed incomes with few options to buy a new home, leaving them looking to their next municipal representative, who also holds a seat at Peel Regional Council, for clear transition commitments. Mississauga.com says candidates responded to the issue, along with other hot-button concerns like road safety and density, in emailed statements. Candidate Fonseca told the outlet she has advocated for Twin Pines residents since 2010 and will keep doing so at Peel Regional Council, adding that building more affordable housing elsewhere does not erase the city's responsibility toward residents already there. According to Mississauga.com, Fonseca called for individualized assistance, clear information and appropriate housing choices for those being displaced, saying success should be measured by how well the community is supported through the transition.

items.title: Driver Remained at Scene After Child Struck on Hillcrest Avenue in Cooksville, Police Say
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a child was struck by a vehicle Monday afternoon in Mississauga's Cooksville neighbourhood. According to police, the incident happened on Hillcrest Avenue near Confederation Parkway, just north of Dundas Street East. CTV News reports the driver remained at the scene after the collision. Police told the outlet the child was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. According to police, the investigation is ongoing, and anyone with further information is asked to contact Peel police or Crime Stoppers.
